text:
The European Commission will on Wednesday present a plan to provide a €45 billion loan to Ukraine backed by headroom in the bloc’s long-term budget, according to two EU officials.
The loan, which would have to be agreed by EU leaders, aims to keep Ukraine financially afloat in the coming year as Moscow ramps up its drone and missile attacks against Ukrainian infrastructure.
The Commission will propose that EU leaders agree to backstop the loan with the headroom in the EU’s current long-term budget, in a similar way to how a previous €90 billion loan was backed by the budget, the officials said.
EU leaders are due to discuss the loan at their next gathering on Nov. 26-27. They will need to agree unanimously to use the headroom, or remaining amounts, in the Multiannual Financial Framework to finance the loan.
Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria have signaled they will not participate in future loans for Ukraine, but in the past these countries did not block using the MFF to backstop Ukraine loans.
